宏福苑火災引起各界關注維修工程圍標問題。競委會今年1月曾搜查14間工程承辦商和顧問公司，涉嫌在全港17個維修工程從事圍標等行為，估計合約總值約七億港元。行動中取得的證據揭發存在另一個圍標集團，競委會今日再搜查4間承辦商，涉及28個大廈維修工程，總值約五億元，涉嫌在投標期間提交「掩護式」標書等。

The Competition Commission announced that yesterday (the 12th), it launched a second round of enforcement action in a bid-rigging case involving building maintenance, searching 12 premises, including the offices of four engineering contractors and the residences of persons involved. The projects in question cover maintenance works for 28 housing estates and buildings, with contract values preliminarily estimated at around HK$500 million. The maintenance projects concerned are spread across 12 districts in Hong Kong, Kowloon and the New Territories, with some contracts not yet awarded and others already commenced or completed before the investigation began.

The Commission pointed out that this operation is a follow-up to the first round of enforcement action in January this year, when 14 engineering contractors and consultancy firms were searched, involving 17 maintenance projects with a total value of around HK$700 million. The Commission stated that among the evidence obtained during that operation, a suspicious telephone message exchange was discovered, suggesting the possible existence of another hidden bid-rigging syndicate intending to target the maintenance works of a certain housing estate. According to the content of the exchange, a contractor that had not previously been investigated was suspected of having used intermediaries during the tendering period of the housing estate project to approach other contractors in order to submit cover bids, but received replies indicating that some contractors had already been recruited by others to take part in bid-rigging for the same project.

After analysis, the Commission found that the contractor was suspected of engaging in anti-competitive conduct across multiple projects, including distributing so-called "homework" bid price instructions to other contractors to manipulate tender outcomes. The alleged conduct may constitute bid-rigging, market sharing, price-fixing conspiracies and the exchange of sensitive information, in violation of the Competition Ordinance, prompting enforcement action against the contractor, other contractors involved and related persons. In addition to searching the premises, the parties were also required to produce documents and materials, and to attend hearings to provide relevant information. The Commission stated it would be inappropriate at this stage to disclose the targets of the investigation or case details.
